verdict: Not ready to ship: the validator creation cell contains a quoting error that raises a SyntaxError and prevents the validator from running, plus a few content/pedagogical issues to tighten before shipping.
blockers: Cell 17 writes an invalid Python file due to nested triple-quote usage in the string literal (SyntaxError). This prevents the validator from being created and run.

findings.text: The validator source is constructed with a triple-quoted Python string that itself contains an unescaped triple-quoted docstring ("""), which prematurely ends the outer string literal and causes a SyntaxError when the cell runs. Fix by using a different quoting strategy (e.g., outer triple single quotes '''...''' or escape/concatenate the inner docstring) or by writing the file from a template file.

location.label: Run the validator script and parse its JSON

findings.text: This cell fails as a direct consequence of the broken validator file (cell 17). Until the validator file is fixed, the subprocess call will return an error / missing output and the subsequent assert will fail. Address the SyntaxError in cell 17 first.

The generated instructions use the placeholder package name 'my_package' throughout. The notebook should explicitly call out that learners must replace 'my_package' with their repository's actual top-level package name (or show how to detect it automatically) to avoid producing misleading instructions.

Heading-detection logic compares heading starts using startswith() which is pragmatic but could produce false positives (e.g., headings like 'Purpose and scope' still pass). Consider matching whole-heading tokens or documenting that partial matches are intended.

The FORBIDDEN regex includes re.compile(r"PASSWORD") and a comment 'case-sensitive by design to reduce FPs'. This will miss common lowercase forms like 'password'. Either document this design decision prominently or use case-insensitive matching and add heuristics to reduce false positives.

The markdown sanity check counts code-fence occurrences with md.count('```') and requires evenness. This is reasonable but fragile for inline backticks or fenced blocks using ~~~. Consider supporting both fence styles or using a Markdown parser for robust checks.

location.label: git add/commit (skips safely if not in a repo or git missing)

findings.text: The commit logic uses 'git diff --cached --quiet' and checks returncode; that's fine, but the code doesn't surface git errors (e.g., if add fails due to permission). Consider printing add.stdout/add.stderr on failure (the cell already prints stderr for add/commit failures, but be explicit).
